title: Weekly links July 23: a causal inference checklist, lessons from innovation RCTs, long-term impacts are hard to measure, and more…
gist: A development-economics links roundup whose signal is concentrated in three items: 29 IGL innovation RCTs showing intervention impacts are unpredictable from theory and benign programs can backfire; long-run SME follow-ups where outcome variance far exceeded power-calculation assumptions; and Anthropic's new $200 million Economic Futures Research Fund writing $5-30 million grants with a $1 million floor.

insights.claim: Scott Cunningham has published a 12-step checklist for non-experimental causal inference projects, framed as useful both for identifying where treatment variation comes from and for building into an AI pipeline.
insights.so_what: Signals that structured causal-inference workflows are being codified for AI automation — a template for automating quant research review.
insights.quote: useful suggestions for understanding where the treatment variation is coming from, and for building into an AI pipeline
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs

insights.claim: The single biggest lesson across a portfolio of 29 randomized trials on innovation, start-ups, entrepreneurship and firms is that intervention impacts cannot be predicted from theory alone, making rigorous testing essential.
insights.so_what: Discount theory-driven claims about accelerator and SME-support program efficacy absent trial evidence.
insights.quote: we can’t predict the impacts of an intervention from theory alone. Rigorous testing of the impacts is crucial.
insights.locator: IGL blog on lessons from 29 RCTs
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs

insights.claim: Evidence from innovation RCTs indicates people can be nudged into acting as innovators, implying entrepreneurial behavior is partly malleable rather than fixed by type.
insights.so_what: Supports low-cost behavioral interventions in innovation policy over pure selection-based programs.
insights.quote: People can be nudged into acting as innovators
insights.locator: IGL blog on lessons from 29 RCTs
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs

insights.claim: Innovation-program evaluation should treat 'rational quitting' — participants shutting down a venture — as a potentially positive outcome rather than a program failure.
insights.so_what: Changes how to read startup-program KPIs: survival rates can mislead about program value.
insights.quote: “Rational quitting” can be a positive outcome
insights.locator: IGL blog on lessons from 29 RCTs
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs

insights.claim: Entrepreneurs do not always know what they need, and matching the type of support to the actual needs of the individual or business can be crucial to whether business support works.
insights.so_what: Demand-led program design can misallocate; diagnostic matching is the value-add in business support services.
insights.quote: Entrepreneurs don’t always know what they need
insights.locator: IGL blog on lessons from 29 RCTs
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs

insights.claim: Benign-sounding interventions in firm and entrepreneurship support can produce unintended negative effects.
insights.so_what: Downside risk is real in SME-support policy — treat unevaluated programs as having ambiguous sign, not zero floor.
insights.quote: Benign-sounding interventions can have unintended negative effects.
insights.locator: IGL blog on lessons from 29 RCTs
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs

themes.theme: Long-run outcome variance breaks evaluation power

insights.claim: Longer-term follow-ups of business support programs found participant firms diverging over the 4-5 years after participation from complete shutdown to superstar high-growth companies, with variation far higher than the interim data used for the original power calculations assumed.
insights.so_what: Interim-data power calculations systematically understate outcome variance — treat null results from long-horizon SME trials as weak evidence of no effect.
insights.quote: businesses went on to widely diverging fates, from shutting down entirely to becoming superstar high-growth companies
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs

insights.claim: The more variable and unpredictable long-run outcomes are, the lower an evaluation's statistical power and the higher the risk of failing to detect a true difference between participant and comparison SMEs.
insights.so_what: A methodological caution for reading impact-evaluation literature: absence of significance in high-variance settings is uninformative.
insights.quote: The more variable and unpredictable are outcomes, the lower the statistical power
insights.locator: Second, there are powerful methodological implications
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs

insights.claim: Measuring outcomes over longer timescales is necessary to capture both the true potential and the pitfalls of business-support interventions, since short-horizon results miss divergence.
insights.so_what: Argues for multi-year measurement horizons — relevant to how development finance institutions should judge SME portfolio impact.
insights.locator: First, it highlights the importance of measuring outcomes
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs

insights.claim: Anthropic's Economic Futures Research Fund has launched with $200 million to support ambitious interventions preparing society for the economic impact of AI, seeking large-scale RCTs and creative pilots or program evaluations.
insights.so_what: A $200m private research pool reshapes the AI-labor-impact evidence base and the incentives of development economists.
insights.locator: Anthropic’s Economic Futures Research Fund has launched
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs

insights.claim: The Anthropic fund plans to primarily fund projects in the $5-30 million range, is flexible upward for well-scoped high-potential proposals, and will not directly fund anything below $1 million.
insights.so_what: Grant-size floor pushes the field toward consortium-scale projects — smaller labs get squeezed out or must aggregate.
insights.quote: We plan to primarily fund projects in the $5-30 million range
insights.locator: we want to fund the most ambitious proposals possible
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs

insights.claim: Peter McCrory, Head of Economics at Anthropic, has published an essay arguing why AI has not increased U.S. unemployment so far.
insights.so_what: An AI-lab insider pushing back on AI-displacement narratives is a signal for anyone trading the AI-labor-disruption theme.
insights.quote: an interesting essay by Peter McCrory, the Head of Economics at Anthropic on why AI hasn’t increased U.S. unemployment so far
insights.locator: see also an interesting essay by Peter McCrory
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs

insights.claim: The World Bank Research Observer is soliciting policy-relevant development surveys for non-specialist audiences with submissions due by September 30, 2026 for its Fall 2026 editorial board meeting, and a new thinking in industrial policy conference at Columbia University on November 6 has a September 14 submission deadline.
insights.so_what: Industrial policy is being institutionalized as an academic research agenda — watch these venues for the intellectual pipeline behind future subsidy regimes.
insights.locator: The World Bank Research Observer (WBRO) seeks to publish
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
